title: Add native correction node plugins with optional Python discovery
body:
CorrectionLib currently fixes node types in its C++ variant/parser and Python schema. This adds a native extension node and factory registry so separately installed providers can supply new scalar nodes, with optional discovery through `[project.entry-points."correctionlib.nodes"]`.

The core, SDK, provider and consuming C++ application build and run without Python or pybind11. Native libraries support explicit registration or transactional shared-library loading, with API/build compatibility checks, registry snapshots and retained library ownership. Python adapters use those same native implementations. Recursive schema/CLI validation, pickle restoration, independently packaged CMake/wheel examples, documentation and tests are included.

Validation:
- Local Python-free AlmaLinux build root with pybind11 absent: independently build/install core and provider, build/run a third-project consumer, and pass both native suites. Covers nesting, malformed configurations, versions, API/build mismatch, rollback, precision, lifetimes and concurrent evaluation.
- Locally installed core/provider wheels: 57 Python tests passed; one optional Dask test skipped and 267 CVMFS cases excluded.
- Final targeted GitHub workflow is fully green: Python-free Debian container; installed-provider integration on Linux (Python 3.9 and 3.13), macOS (3.13), and Windows (3.13).
- On the preceding implementation revision, the pinned formatting/type-check job, full Python build/test matrix and ROOT bindings passed. Its CVMFS job failed during pytest setup with `Function._nodeid` errors; that existing integration issue remains outside the readability pass.

CI follow-ups handle Python 3.9 metadata discovery, Windows CLI test encoding, formatter output, and a Python-3.9-compatible Pydantic constraint in the type-check hook.

This is an experimental C++ SDK requiring compatible core headers/toolchain, not a stable cross-compiler C ABI. Extended schema-v2 payloads require this fork. Native diagnostics identify type/version/correction; full subtree paths are currently added only by Python discovery. Graph-wide batching, multiple outputs and performance benchmarking are outside this change. No merge or upstream PR is requested.

Readability follow-up (`8dc0b7a`): added focused native lifetime/locking/validation/transaction comments, SDK and example explanations, and grouped native test intent with clearer spacing. All eight changed C++ files retain identical code tokens and literal contents after excluding comments/whitespace. A fresh Release build with Python disabled passes both native CTest suites. The header fingerprint includes comment text, so host and providers were rebuilt together. CI is rerunning for this update.

title: Add native batch evaluation for C++ inputs and external nodes
body:
- Add `Correction::evaluate_batch` and typed borrowed input columns, with scalar broadcasting, signed element strides, empty-batch validation and caller-owned output buffers. Python arrays now enter native batch dispatch.
- Add root Binning/MultiBinning column kernels and a provider batch callback with a scalar fallback. A separately compiled probe throws on scalar evaluation and succeeds through the batch callback, proving actual dispatch. Other graph paths preserve scalar fallback.
- Depend on native-node PR #1 at `8dc0b7a8bfe82c15115ff2a5907d4bfa35ee4710`; this PR targets `codex/node-plugins` and does not include array-output implementation. Experimental SDK API 2 and changed header fingerprints require rebuilding providers; API 1 binaries are rejected.
- Validation in WSL2 atlas_al9 / AnalysisBase 25.2.100 / GCC 15.2: 185 Python tests passed, one optional ROOT test skipped, CVMFS tests excluded. Three native suites pass in Release and in a Python-free AddressSanitizer/UBSan/float-cast build, with an independently built provider and separately packaged example.
- Retain matched native and full-Python-call synthetic benchmarks for N=1..16/1000/10000/100000, seven raw rounds, exact checks, machine/compiler metadata and source/binary hashes under `evidence/batches`. Native and Python controls have different timing scopes; no historical speedup claim is made.

API contract and C++/Python examples: `docs/native-batches.md`. Evidence, commands, timer definitions and limitations: `evidence/batches/README.md`. Progress and remaining integration work: `progress.txt`.

This PR is intentionally left open. Integration into develop is separate; no merge into the target branch or upstream is requested.

Implementation and benchmark evidence identify `aa7c819d86786cf613abedc5e73704bc840150dc`; the current documentation also shows Python/C++ batch calls and a complete node with an optional batch callback. Dedicated Native batches and Node plugins checks pass; the final full CI format gate and ROOT/Linux checks pass, with the broader matrix still running at the latest audit. Normal develop merges integrate this head with PR #1 and the independently based array-output PR. The combination uses SDK API 4 and has separate retained evidence; this PR remains API 2.

Published integration: [develop](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/tree/develop), [combined API/examples](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/blob/develop/docs/batch-array-integration.md), [retained evidence](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/tree/develop/evidence/combined), [green integration CI](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/actions/runs/41083592693). Remote ancestry of all three exact feature heads was verified; master and the original plugin branch were not changed.

title: Add fixed array outputs with schema-v3 graph and plugin validation
body:
- Add fixed numeric component outputs for one input point: schema v3 declares `output.shape: [S]`, and explicit `array` nodes evaluate ordered scalar components. Existing schema-v2 scalar payloads remain supported. No scalar-to-array broadcast or reserved systematic labels are introduced.
- Preserve C++ `double evaluate` for scalar corrections and add explicit `evaluate_array` methods. Python returns `(S,)` for scalar inputs and `broadcast_shape + (S,)` for NumPy inputs. Histograms, categories, defaults, flows and Transform content preserve shape; unsupported graph combinations and array CompoundCorrection stacks fail at construction.
- Add array-valued external provider contracts, declared extension output shapes, owning child handles and independent CMake provider examples. Experimental SDK API 3 and header fingerprints require rebuilding all providers. This PR depends on native-node PR #1 at `8dc0b7a8bfe82c15115ff2a5907d4bfa35ee4710`, targets `codex/node-plugins`, and contains no native batch implementation.
- Validation in WSL2 atlas_al9 / AnalysisBase 25.2.100 / GCC 15.2: 146 Python tests passed, ROOT unavailable (one skipped), CVMFS excluded. Three Release native suites and three Python-free ASan/UBSan/float-cast suites passed, including independently compiled array providers. Ruff passed. Mypy 1.19.1 passes all 13 project source files with Python 3.13; the configured Python-3.9 run encounters newer installed uproot syntax, retained in the logs.
- Validate S=1/2/16 and N=1..16/1000/10000/100000, malformed/ragged shapes, mixed branches, empty/strided/broadcast inputs, boundaries, nonfinite inputs, flow, lifetime/pickle/thread behavior and provider shape mismatches. Retain seven matched timing rounds per case, separate native and full Python-call scopes, exact checks and build/machine provenance in `evidence/arrays`.

Payloads, C++/Python examples and contracts: `docs/array-outputs.md`. Reproduction, timing scope, results and limitations: `evidence/arrays/README.md`. Awkward/Dask-Awkward array outputs, ragged/higher-rank outputs and array arithmetic are explicitly unsupported in this version.

This PR remains open. [Develop](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/tree/develop) integrates both features with batch-array wiring. Its dedicated integration CI passed, including independent providers and a Python-free native build. This PR remains open and unmerged.

Implementation and benchmark evidence identify `0b4c7bc1f96e04fa288fa498a29819d3352a44ce`; the current documentation also includes a simple Python/C++ scalar-versus-array comparison for one input point. Dedicated Array outputs and Node plugins checks pass; the final full CI format gate and ROOT/Linux checks pass, with the broader matrix still running at the latest audit. Normal develop merges integrate this head with PR #1 and the independently based batch-input PR. The combination uses SDK API 4 and has separate retained evidence; this PR remains API 3.

Published integration: [develop](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/tree/develop), [combined API/examples](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/blob/develop/docs/batch-array-integration.md), [retained evidence](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/tree/develop/evidence/combined), [green integration CI](https://github.com/gordonwatts/correctionlib/actions/runs/41083592693). Remote ancestry of all three exact feature heads was verified; master and the original plugin branch were not changed.
